costs_stated_before_the_answer: the executor both spends the allowance and holds the count; a record on GitHub makes a change visible, not impossible - weaker than a ledger on the owner's machine

the session's egress proxy re-terminates TLS, so the client verifies the proxy's certificate rather than SEC's and the saved bytes pass through Anthropic's proxy; every acquisition record states the transport
the approval body names the ledger root on the owner's machine and has to be rewritten; the executor must not create a same-named directory in the container to pass the gate's path comparison
requests leave from a shared egress address; if SEC throttles it the run stops by name at a 403 or 429, never beyond the cap, and may take more than one run

checked_before_the_answer.egress_policy: the session's proxy answered '200 Connection Established' to CONNECT requests for www.sec.gov, data.sec.gov and api.deepseek.com; nothing was sent to SEC or to the provider

changes: the ledger root moves into the VM; the new approval body names it

a one-time start marker: when the ledger is initialized the executor writes a random number beside it and posts a marker comment carrying that number on issue 47; the live path reads issue 47's comments from GitHub whenever it opens a session and refuses unless the earliest marker for this approval is unedited, written with OWNER association and carries the local number - so a lost container, or a local ledger deleted together with the files beside it, cannot start the allowance again; resumption is the owner's decision
after each company the executor exports the ledger and the acquired sources and commits and pushes them
the approval comment is read through GitHub's REST API where gh is absent; gh is still used where it exists

the proposal tool regenerates the approval body: the cap [0, 0, 1354] and every grant unchanged, only the ledger root changed, with the execution environment and the durability stated; the owner still posts it byte for byte
model calls run in the VM, with their ledger root in the VM and the same start marker
the executor tells the owner when the provider key is needed
section 3 of the 2026-09-28 contract change: the re-seal before any real call is done by the executor in the VM instead of by the owner on the owner's machine
MODEL_CALLS_RUN_IN_THE_EXECUTOR_VM.unchanged: the call application's decisions and the owner's posted approval are still required before any call

corrections.recorded: 2026-09-29, by the executor after an independent review of the VM change (docs/evidence/issue47_history/model-egress/independent-review-2026-09-29-vm/, findings F1, F2, F4, F10); the decisions above are unchanged, and the original text above is kept as it was written
what_was_overstated: 'the executor's own approval does not count' and the start marker's guarantee held for the executor's code path, not for the executor: in the VM the executor chooses the GitHub reader, the proxy and the CA bundle the read-back goes through, and holds the provider key; the reviewer made the gate accept a never-posted comment with a three-line fake gh

'a lost container, or a local ledger deleted together with the files beside it, cannot start the allowance again': the marker as first built carried the local number, so copying it back beside an empty root matched, and the same request was sent twice (reproduced end to end on the LIVE path)
what_holds_now: the marker carries only a digest of the local start record, so a new container cannot rebuild the start from it

once the branch carries this approval's export a start refuses, and the live path refuses a ledger behind that export; an export only moves forward and a restore refuses beside a surviving start record
before the first export is pushed, a lost container whose marker comment is deleted has no guard; the executor acts on GitHub as the owner's account and can delete it

the gates guard against accidents and make the owner's decision auditable; the controls that bind the executor are outside the code: a dedicated provider key with a provider-side credit limit, revoked after the run, and the committed exports compared with the provider's usage log (SEC: the cap is enforced by the executor's code path only; the exports and the SEC request log are what the owner can check)
